newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Dec 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Dec 27.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page Friday:

- Defying increased pressure from President Slobodan Milosevic to stay off the streets, tens of thousands of opposition demonstrators poured into central Belgrade, apparently energized rather than cowed by the heavy police presence.
- The number of American households investing in mutual funds has risen by more than 20 percent in the last two years.

- As controversy has grown over Democratic fund raising, President Bill Clinton has sought to distinguish between the practices of his own reelection campaign and those of the Democratic National Committee.
- America's fledgling Radio Free Asia is beset by logistical problems that result in few being able to hear the broadcasts.
- The Irish Republican Army in 1983 plotted to kill Prince Charles and the Princess of Wales.

- In a decision that has forced the cancellation of at least 10 research projects, a New York State appeals court has found the state's rules governing psychiatric experiments on children and the mentaly ill to be unconstitutional.
- Some 36 groups of parents and educators hope to take advantage of New Jersey's new charter school law to join one of the fastest-growing movements for school change in the nation.
